_instructions: Copy this file, replace every <FILL IN ...> value, then run: python -m datasets.gold.rubric_check <your file> --dataset datasets/c3_phase3_v5_repaired_v2
The 'rubric' object is exactly the marking engine's Rubric (app/schemas/marking.py): rubric -> criteria -> scoring_levels. Marks come only from the 'mark' of a level.
Give every criterion at least 3 levels, including a 0-mark level and a level worth the criterion's max_marks; criterion max_marks must add up to the question's marks.
Write descriptors a marker can apply without the tier or any model output: say what the answer must show to sit on that level.
Positive levels need required_concepts (on the level or on the criterion) so the same rubric can later be run through the engine.

provenance.status: use 'ai_drafted' for any rubric that an AI tool drafted or helped draft. Only a lecturer who has reviewed it may set 'lecturer_validated', with their name and the review date. Do not set it on someone else's behalf.
The checker verifies that the record is complete and consistent. It cannot verify that a review really took place.
